papers.version_note: arXiv v1, 13 Aug 2022. Matches the record.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, sections II to V (architecture, mesh correction, weak nonlinearities, discussion). Methods and supplementary parts not read in detail.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of how fabrication loss, imperfect couplers and weak Kerr nonlinearities limit trainable quantum photonic neural networks, benchmarked on a Bell-state analyzer.

assertions.value: The authors report that a quantum photonic neural network fabricated with current state-of-the-art processes, with a sub-optimal effective Kerr nonlinearity, can act as a Bell-state analyzer with an unconditional fidelity of 0.891, rising to 0.999999 if success is conditioned on detecting a photon in each logical photonic qubit.
quotes: can achieve an unconditional fidelity of 0.891, that increases to 0.999999 if it is possible to precondition success on the detection of a photon in each logical photonic qubit.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical (simulated) result from one study with its stated component model.
assertions.reader_inference: The result comes from numerical simulation with modeled imperfections, not from a fabricated device.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for a given set of fabrication imperfections and effective nonlinearity, there is an optimal network size: adding layers tends to raise the conditional fidelity, but the probability of a computational basis output falls exponentially.
assertions.anchor: Abstract and Section IV, pages 1 and 5
quotes: we demonstrate that there is an optimal network size, which balances imperfections versus the ability to compensate for lacking nonlinearities.
While adding layers will always tend to increase F (con), a balance must be struck with the exponential decrease in P(cb).
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study; the paper adds one more example (GHZ state) in its supplement.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in their model of a realistic mesh, the transmittance of each directional coupler is randomly selected from a normal distribution with a mean of 50% and a standard deviation of 5.08%.
quotes: randomly selected from a normal distribution with a mean of 50% and standard deviation of 5.08%
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own simulation setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that operating with weaker nonlinearities decreases the probability that the network converges to the loss limit during training.
quotes: operating with weaker nonlinearities decreases the probability that the QPNN converges at the loss limit during training
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit on its result.

papers.title_in_file: Squeezing as a resource for time series processing in quantum reservoir computing
papers.version_note: arXiv v2, 16 Oct 2023. Matches the record.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, sections III to V (tasks under noise, accessible memory, conclusion). Appendices not read.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of how squeezing in a loop-based photonic quantum reservoir affects time series processing under readout noise.

assertions.value: The authors report that multimode squeezing enhances the accessible memory of the photonic quantum reservoir and improves performance in several benchmark temporal tasks.
quotes: We demonstrate that multimode squeezing enhances its accessible memory, which improves the performance in several benchmark temporal tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical (simulated) result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that squeezing can be either detrimental or beneficial for quantum reservoir computing when moving from ideal to realistic models that include experimental noise, and that its effect under measurement noise deviates completely from predictions under ideal conditions.
assertions.anchor: Abstract and Section V, pages 1 and 7
quotes: squeezing can be either detrimental or beneficial for quantum reservoir computing when moving from ideal to realistic models, accounting for experimental noise.
the effect of squeezing on the QRC performance when accounting for measurement noise completely deviates from predictions under ideal conditions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical (simulated) result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Results under idealized noiseless models may not carry over to noisy quantum reservoirs.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the Mackey-Glass chaotic time series, under additive noise, the squeezed (active) cavity reservoir predicts much better than the passive one over the long term, achieving accurate predictions up to 50 time steps.
quotes: We see that the active cavity performs a much better prediction than the passive one in the long term, achieving accurate predictions up to 50 time steps.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical (simulated) result from one task.

assertions.value: The authors state that readout noise is theoretically unavoidable in quantum reservoirs because of the stochastic nature of quantum measurements, and that the resulting statistical fluctuations can hinder any possible quantum advantage.
quotes: readout noise is theoretically unavoidable due to the stochastic nature of quantum measurements, which produce statistical fluctuations that can hinder any possible quantum advantage
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement supported by citations, not shown in this paper.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Algorithm for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
papers.version_note: arXiv v1, 18 Apr 2023. Matches the record.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section III overview and complexity summaries, conclusion. Step-by-step circuit derivations skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theoretical quantum version of the Local Outlier Factor anomaly detection algorithm with a complexity analysis against the classical algorithm.

assertions.value: The paper shows, by complexity analysis, that the proposed quantum Local Outlier Factor algorithm achieves exponential speedup on the dimension of the data points and polynomial speedup on the number of data points compared to its classical counterpart.
quotes: It is shown that our quantum algorithm achieves exponential speedup on the dimension of the data points and polynomial speedup on the number of data points compared to its classical counterpart.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical complexity derivation by the authors, conditional on the QRAM and parameter assumptions in the next assertions.
assertions.reader_inference: The text I read contains no experiment or hardware run; the claim rests on asymptotic analysis alone.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithm takes the data matrix as stored in a QRAM, and that the parameter k is assumed to be given in advance.
quotes: Input: Data matrix X stored in a QRAM.
Here we assume that the parameter k is given in advance.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and assumptions.
assertions.reader_inference: The speedup claim depends on QRAM access, which is an assumption about hardware not yet available.

assertions.value: The authors state that the choice of parameter k is crucial to the performance of such algorithms, but that how to choose a suitable k is outside the scope of their discussion.
quotes: The choice of parameter k is crucial to the performance of such algorithms, but how to choose a suitable k is outside the scope of our discussion.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a scope limit.

papers.title_in_file: Automatic and effective discovery of quantum kernels
papers.version_note: The file name says Structure-Learning-of-Quantum-Embeddings (the 2022 v1 title), but the file content is arXiv 2209.11144v3 dated 26 Dec 2024, titled Automatic and effective discovery of quantum kernels. It matches the record title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section IV experiments and results, section V conclusions, supplementary note on optimizer and criteria. Mathematical background skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A method that searches automatically for quantum kernel circuits with a meta-heuristic optimizer, tested on a high-energy-physics anomaly detection task.

assertions.value: The authors report that, on a high-energy-physics anomaly detection problem, their automated search can in the best-case scenario either match or improve testing accuracy relative to the manual design approach.
quotes: demonstrate that, in the best-case scenario, we can either match or improve testing accuracy with respect to the manual design approach
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one task family.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract's wording, best-case scenario, signals selective reporting of the favorable configurations.

assertions.value: The authors report that with 12 operations their method outperforms both classical and quantum kernels on the Narrow G and A to HZ datasets, that with a reduced number of operations it finds a kernel with slightly lower accuracy than the state-of-the-art quantum kernel, and that on the more challenging Broad G dataset it outperforms both by a consistent margin.
assertions.anchor: Section IV results, Table I, page 7
quotes: our method with m = 12 operations outperforms both classical and quantum kernels.
our algorithm discovers a kernel with a slightly lower accuracy than the state-of-the-art quantum kernel
our algorithm discovers a kernel able to outperform both classical and quantum kernels by a consistent margin.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; the per-dataset figures are in Table I and not quoted here.

assertions.value: The authors state that candidate kernels are evaluated with a one-class SVM using separate training and testing sets of 200 and 1500 elements, respectively, and that the testing is repeated five times with different i.i.d. test samples.
quotes: We use separate training and testing sets, consisting of 200 and 1500 elements, respectively.
The testing process is repeated five times, each with a different i.i.d. samples testing set of 1500 elements
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own evaluation setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that they present only a limited subset of the possible configurations, and that the experiment is limited by an arbitrary choice of optimizer, fixed to Bayesian optimization.
assertions.anchor: Section V and supplementary note, pages 7 and 14
quotes: we have only presented here a limited subset of the possible configurations.
The experiment presented in Section IV is limited by the arbitrary choice of the optimizer, which has been fixed to Bayesian optimization
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its limits.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning Implementations: Proposals and Experiments
papers.version_note: arXiv v1, 11 Mar 2023. Matches the record.
papers.what_it_is: A short review and perspective on quantum reinforcement learning, quantum autoencoders and quantum memristors, and their experiments on photonic and superconducting platforms.

assertions.value: The author states that the article is not a thorough account of the literature and focuses on three proposals with their quantum experiments: quantum reinforcement learning, quantum autoencoders, and quantum memristors.
quotes: We will focus on three proposals and their respective quantum experiments: quantum reinforcement learning, quantum autoencoders, and quantum memristors.
With this article we do not intend to give a thorough account of the existing literature
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope.

assertions.value: The author reports, describing an experiment by others, that a photonic quantum reinforcement learning experiment achieved large fidelities even with few iterations, and in some cases performed better than a standard quantum tomography protocol, with evidence of this when quantum resources are limited.
quotes: The experimental realization showed that, even with few iterations of the protocol, large fidelities could be achieved, and in some cases one could have a better performance than with just a standard quantum tomography protocol
evidence was obtained that this would take place when the quantum resources are limited
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited experimental result from other work, summarized by a review.

assertions.value: The author states that the field could be among the first quantum technologies to produce results beneficial to industry and society, and that near-term proof-of-principle experiments may already show some evidence of speedup with respect to classical algorithms.
quotes: The field of quantum machine learning could be among the first quantum technologies producing results that are beneficial for industry and, in turn, to society.
principle quantum machine learning experiments that may already show some evidence of speedup with respect to classical algorithms
assertions.certainty_reason: An author perspective, hedged with could and may, without evidence in this paper.

papers.title_in_file: Fitting a Collider in a Quantum Computer: Tackling the Challenges of Quantum Machine Learning for Big Datasets
papers.version_note: arXiv v4, 6 Dec 2023 (file name year 2022 is the v1 year). Matches the record.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, dataset and feature selection sections, simulation results, discrete-variable follow-up, real-hardware section. Appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A benchmark of variational quantum classifiers against shallow classical models on a high-energy-physics signal-versus-background task, with feature and data reduction.

assertions.value: The authors report that the performance of the quantum algorithms was comparable to the classical ones, that no case was found where QML outperforms any of the shallow methods tested, and that the best QML result, from the TPE optimizer, was an AUC score of 0.841.
quotes: The performance of the quantum algorithms was found to be comparable to the classical ones, even when using large datasets.
It was also observed that there are no cases where QML outperforms any of the shallow methods tested.
The TPE optimizer regime produced the best performance for QML, achieving an AUC score of 0.841
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one dataset, mostly in simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a no-advantage result on a realistic classification task, useful as a counterweight to advantage claims.

assertions.value: The authors state that embedding each of the 47 features would need 47 qubits, which is impractical on currently available quantum computers, so they considered quantum computers with only 5 qubits and reduced the features.
quotes: 47 qubits would be needed to train a VQC using all the dataset features.
Such number of qubits is impractical given the currently available quantum computers and thus it is not feasible to train a VQC using all the features in our dataset.
quantum computers with only 5 qubits were considered
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope limit.

assertions.value: The authors report that QML circuits trained on features from sequential backward selection were generally unstable and sensitive to fluctuations in the sampled data, with PCA-derived data giving significantly more stable results, and that excluding discrete variables improved performance in a limited study of 2 features.
assertions.anchor: Section 8 and discrete-variable follow-up, pages 17 and 25
quotes: QML circuits trained with SBS data are generally unstable and very susceptible to fluctuations in the randomly sampled data
using PCA-originated data produces significantly more stable results.
we found that excluding discrete variables during feature selection led to better performance for VQC circuits in a limited study of 2 features
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; the authors call the discrete-variable test limited.

assertions.value: The authors report that the best-performing TPE-trained circuit was run on six different IBM quantum systems with identical architectures, with no error mitigation, and that the results were compatible with the simulated ones.
quotes: This VQC was implemented and its test set was inferred on six different quantum systems with identical architectures, all freely available.
Since the implemented circuits are small, no error mitigation techniques were implemented.
The obtained results, shown in Figure 13, are compatible with the simulated ones
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small circuit on freely available hardware.

assertions.value: The authors propose a framework to identify and recommend the best-suited solution paths for quantum-assisted optimization in an automated way, and state that they demonstrate and validate it on a selected set of options, illustrated on the capacitated vehicle routing problem.
quotes: We propose a framework designed to identify and recommend the best-suited solution paths in an automated way.
We demonstrate and validate our approach on a selected set of options and illustrate its application on the capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP).
assertions.certainty_reason: An author-reported demonstration on selected example options.

assertions.value: The authors state that the workflow has been implemented on a selection of example problems with a subset of options at every level, with an initial recommendation, and that hardware and compiler options are not included.
quotes: The envisioned workflow has been implemented on a selection of example problems by populating all levels with a subset of options among which an initial recommendation is given.
Only hardware and compiler options are not included
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own implementation scope.
